A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenRecal, with matching authors, architecture, and principal experiments. All pages, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison. Material was matched across the layout change, including the relocated dataset description and the removal of v1 Appendices G–H.

before.justification: v1 reports original GenRecal benchmark results, teacher–student comparisons, regularization ablations, representation analyses, and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Table 5 with computational measurements, ablations, cross-tokenizer comparisons, and additional LLM/VLM evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the two-decoder Recalibrator, pre/post projections, mixed student-question/teacher-answer features, alignment regularization, and three-stage training. Positional re-embedding already appears in v1. Expanded explanations and corrected KL pseudocode clarify the existing logit-based procedure; they do not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Table 5(g) adds text-only LLM distillation evaluated on MMLU, GPQA, and MATH, substantially extending the original vision-language task coverage. The original visual benchmarks and 9M training-data mixture remain; their dataset description moves to Appendix F.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds evaluated ULD and MOT cross-tokenizer baselines, InternVL2.5 teacher/student SFT controls, and additional LLM and VLM baselines. Conversely, v1 Appendix G's answer-only MiniLLM, DistiLLM, and LLaVA-KD comparisons disappear. Their original same-token comparisons remain in Table 4.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported setup from 256 to 8 A100 GPUs and effective batches from 16K/8K to 512/256. New experiments vary Recalibrator depth, training sample counts, positional embedding, teacher fine-tuning, and model pairings; the answer-only experiment is removed. These are reported setting changes, without evidence establishing reruns of the retained results.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds analyses of computational overhead, decoder depth, positional re-embedding, dataset scale, and SFT effects. These examine efficiency and design choices beyond v1's regularization and dataset-composition analyses, which remain. The answer-only distillation analysis from v1 Appendix G is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies independent-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results continue reporting point estimates; Table 5's averages summarize benchmark scores rather than uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical numerical results, while Table 5 adds substantial new results. For example, Table 5(f) reports four-benchmark averages of 69.4 for ULD, 70.8 for MOT, and 76.4 for GenRecal. Additional ablation and compatibility scores are new, while Appendix G's answer-only scores are removed; these are not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix E corrects the KL expression in Algorithms 1–3: the second operand changes from the hidden feature r_al to VLM-head_l(r_al), repairing the written loss definition. The newly displayed main-text equations otherwise restate existing computations; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims of general-purpose distillation across heterogeneous token types, efficient student VLMs, and competitive benchmark performance. Removing one contribution bullet and replacing 'compatible' with 'agnostic' do not materially change those claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations supporting two decoder blocks and a practical 5M training subset, and attributes cross-tokenizer baseline weaknesses to padding/truncation and token matching. It removes Appendix G's qualification that answer-only distillation can accommodate different image embeddings when text tokenizers match. The original feature-alignment and regularization explanations remain.

D1.justification: The hardware and batch-size disclosures change substantially. v2 also removes gradient-checkpointing and LoRA implementation details, including rank/alpha 64 and dropout 0.05, and drops the project-page link. It adds Recalibrator parameter/FLOP information and clarifies regularization propagation in Appendix E. Omitted optimization details do not establish that the underlying techniques were abandoned.

R1.justification: v2 adds word-embedding alignment literature as motivation, cites MOT and additional model papers, and directly positions GenRecal against cross-tokenizer methods. ULD was already cited in v1, so its publication-version citation is not a new research work. Some references disappear with removed material, while the broader related-work account remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanation, training description, and extended related work undergo extensive rewriting. Validation and Recalibrator analysis are merged, computational analysis and a separate discussion are introduced, and the conclusion is separated. Dataset documentation moves to Appendix F, while Appendices G–H are removed.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive figure/table repositioning and resizing. Figure 1 moves before the abstract, a nine-panel Table 5 is added, and the Appendix G table disappears. Existing plots and diagrams are largely reused rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The new cross-tokenizer comparisons and controls for depth, positional encoding, data scale, and SFT strengthen empirical support, while corrected KL pseudocode improves technical clarity. These gains are tempered by removal of the informative answer-only comparison, optimization details, and project link. The unexplained GPU/batch-size revision alongside unchanged Tables 1–4 also leaves reproducibility questions, limiting the overall improvement.
